page: Amazon Web Services c8i.48xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. The hardware is driven by a 96-core, 192-thread Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor operating at 3.9 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. CPU resources are dedicated rather than shared, backed by a large 480 MB L3 cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 48 KB L1d cache. Memory capacity totals 384.0 GB of DDR5 operating at 7 GHz, providing a 2.0 GB memory-to-vCPU allocation tailored for compute-heavy profiles. Network connectivity offers a baseline throughput of 75 Gbps. The instance includes no bundled local storage and contains zero discrete GPUs.

The instance incorporates Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX tile and int8) alongside AVX-512 vector instruction sets, benefiting matrix math and vector calculations. Benchmark testing highlights top-tier multi-threaded processing power, evidenced by a multi-core stress-ng score of 207,552.8, a Geekbench multi-core score of 23,119.0, and a PassMark CPU score of 143,522.82. Memory subsystems demonstrate high throughput, achieving 586.09 GB/sec on uncached large-block reads and 250.45 GB/sec on writes. In application-focused metrics, the platform scored 69,143.0 in Clang software compilation and 270.56 million operations per second in Redis SET tests, alongside top-tier LLM prompt processing speeds across small, medium, and large models.

Resource allocation delivers dense computing throughput per instance, though single-core execution speeds fall within average to strong tiers rather than top-tier percentiles. Because local disk storage is absent, persistent storage requirements must be handled over the network. The hardware profile is aligned with high-concurrency multi-threaded applications, including parallel software compilation, distributed Redis caching, CPU-based machine learning inference, and compute-bound simulation workloads.
description: Amazon Web Services c8i.48xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the Nitro hypervisor and powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor with 96 physical cores, 192 dedicated vCPUs, and a 3.9 GHz clock speed. The server features 384.0 GB of high-frequency DDR5 memory running at 7 GHz, maintaining a 2.0 GB per vCPU ratio, paired with 75 Gbps of baseline networking. It contains no onboard local storage and no discrete GPUs. The CPU architecture includes AVX-512 and Intel AMX matrix extensions, delivering top-tier multi-core performance in PassMark, Geekbench, and stress-ng tests. Large-block memory read bandwidth reaches 586.09 GB/sec, assisting data-intensive parallel execution. Operating tradeoffs include moderate single-threaded performance and dependence on network storage for persistent file systems. The system is designed for multi-threaded workloads, including software compilation, CPU-driven LLM prompt processing, in-memory caching, and batch data processing.
